Name: WordPress
Support: Open-source software maintained by the WordPress contributor community. Community support forums and commercial hosting are available.
Technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL or MariaDB. Client: a browser-based block editor for authors and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for visitors.
Capabilities: Authors build posts and pages with blocks. Themes control the design, plugins add features, and the REST API lets other applications work with site content.
Limitations: Installed plugins and themes need ongoing updates. On a self-hosted site, the administrator manages those updates and plans for recovery if an update causes a problem.

Name: Drupal
Support: Open-source software maintained by the Drupal community. The Drupal Association supports the project, and commercial partners offer implementation and support.
Technology: Server: PHP. Database options include MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL. Client: a browser-based editing interface. Twig templates generate HTML for visitors.
Capabilities: Teams can define content types with reusable fields, translate content, and require editorial approval before publishing. Modules extend functionality and themes control presentation.
Limitations: Maintaining contributed modules and themes commonly requires Composer. Updates can involve dependency changes and database updates, so the team needs technical maintenance skills.

Name: Ghost
Support: Open-source software developed by the nonprofit Ghost Foundation and contributors. Ghost(Pro) provides paid managed hosting.
Technology: Server: Node.js. Database: MySQL for supported production installations. Client: a browser-based editor. Handlebars themes generate HTML pages for readers.
Capabilities: Publishers can publish articles, send email newsletters, register members, and restrict selected posts to paying subscribers.
Limitations: Ghost officially supports a narrow production stack. A company that standardizes on PostgreSQL would need to operate a separate MySQL database or use managed hosting.

Name: Wagtail
Support: Open-source software maintained by the Wagtail project and contributors. Community and commercial support are available.
Technology: Server: Python and Django. Database options include PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and SQLite. Client: a browser-based editor. Django templates can render the public pages.
Capabilities: Developers define page types and reusable content blocks. Editors can arrange those blocks, preview pages, schedule publication, and submit changes for approval.
Limitations: Creating a new page type generally requires a developer to define a Python model and a template. Editors depend on the layouts and fields the development team provides.

Name: MediaWiki
Support: Free, open-source wiki software developed by the Wikimedia Foundation and volunteer contributors.
Technology: Server: PHP. Database options include MariaDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. Client: contributors edit through a web browser, and readers view HTML pages.
Capabilities: Contributors can edit shared pages, compare revisions, restore earlier versions, and discuss proposed changes on talk pages. Skins and extensions customize the wiki.
Limitations: Extension compatibility varies by MediaWiki version. An administrator may need to update or replace an extension during an upgrade.

Name: Shopify
Support: Commercial hosted platform developed and supported by Shopify. Shopify maintains the hosting infrastructure and platform software.
Technology: Data layer: Shopify manages product, collection, and page records and exposes them through its admin and APIs. Client layer: merchants use a browser-based admin. Storefront themes use Liquid templates, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
Capabilities: Staff can organize products into collections, publish pages and blog posts, customize storefront themes, and add features through apps. The same platform also handles inventory, checkout, and orders.
Limitations: Some checkout changes depend on the subscription plan. Adding custom interface elements to the information, shipping, or payment steps requires Shopify Plus.

Name: Wix
Support: Commercial hosted platform developed and supported by Wix. Wix manages the hosting and provides a browser-based site editor.
Technology: Data layer: Wix CMS stores records in managed collections with fields and items. Client layer: authors work in a visual browser editor and connect page elements to collection fields through datasets.
Capabilities: Authors can create a collection, design a reusable layout, and generate a page for each item. For example, adding a project record can create a portfolio page with its own title, images, and description.
Limitations: Collection item counts and database storage are limited by the site's plan. A growing directory or catalog may require a plan upgrade.

Name: Joomla
Support: Open-source CMS maintained by the Joomla Project and its contributor community. Site owners can choose their own hosting provider.
Technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Client layer: authors use a browser-based administrator interface, and site templates deliver HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to visitors.
Capabilities: Editors can organize articles into categories, publish in multiple languages, and assign permissions to user groups. Templates control the layout, and extensions add functionality.
Limitations: Self-hosting requires a server that meets Joomla's PHP and database requirements. The site owner must maintain that environment and check extension compatibility when planning upgrades.
